_comment: Dyno -> EKS pod sizing + node selection. Used by the design EKS branch when design_constraints.kubernetes.value is eks-managed or eks-or-ecs. DIRECT LOOKUP: read pod requests/limits + recommended node type per dyno. heroku_cpu_share/heroku_memory_mb provenance is NOT here (pod values are the lookup). Mirrors dyno-fargate-sizing.json's 19 keys.
_on_not_found: reject the formation; produce NO entry; warn 'Unsupported dyno type: {dyno_type}. Cannot map to EKS.'; continue (same as the Fargate path)
_design_rationale: CPU request = dyno CPU share; memory request = dyno memory exactly; CPU limit = 2x request (burst); memory limit = request (avoid OOM). RAM-optimized types use r6i nodes.

_node_size_rank._comment: Rank for 'largest-pod-class-wins' node selection across all formations: pick the node_type of the largest dyno present. Higher rank = larger.

node_sizing._comment: Post-loop, from all EKS formations. system overhead per node = 500m CPU + 512Mi.
node_sizing.instance_type: the node_type of the LARGEST dyno present across all formations (by _node_size_rank; ties keep the first encountered, e.g. m6i.4xlarge over r6i.4xlarge unless a ram-type is the only one at that rank)
node_sizing.total_pods: sum of all EKS formation replicas (quantities)
node_sizing.desired_size: max(min_size, ceil(total_pods / 4))  — clamp UP to min_size; AWS rejects desired < min (matters for small workloads, total_pods <= 4)
node_sizing._pods_per_node: node types are chosen to fit >=4 pods of their dyno class after system overhead

cluster._kubernetes_version_note: DOCUMENTED CONSTANT (port-time decision): EKS deprecates versions on a rolling basis; the DSL makes no AWS calls at design time. Bump this when authoring a new release.
cluster._node_group_note: eks-managed -> self-managed node groups (full K8s control); eks-or-ecs -> managed node groups (less operational burden).
